subject: SLO tolerance & fallback matrix — Summit Bank discovery
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Asha Menon <asha@summitbank.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T15:04:00-08:00
Subject: Discovery follow-up: SLO tolerance & graceful degradation (Summit Bank)

Hi Asha — thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth.

Pain points you shared (short):
- Two production incidents this year where payments flow experienced 20–45 min outages during peak windows (largest: 2026-09-03).
- Current in-house endpoints degrade by returning errors rather than deterministic degraded responses (missing graceful fallback to lightweight models).
- Need predictable latency and a fallback plan that preserves correctness for fraud checks and payment authorization.

Current stack you mentioned: internal GPU-hosted LLMs behind a gateway, no cross-region model routing, limited KV cache reuse, and a proprietary throttling layer.

Success criteria you gave in the call:
- Payment decision path availability >= 99.9% (monthly)
- Degraded-mode responses acceptable if they are deterministic and auditable
- P95 generation latency < 350ms for decisioning endpoints (goal)

Proposed next steps from Redwood (action owners):
1) We’ll send a preliminary SLO tolerance and fallback matrix that maps incident types to fallback behaviors and model tiers (Ben — send by EOD Mon 11/16).
2) Schedule a 60-minute technical deep dive with your infra/ops and security teams to validate routing and KV cache compatibility (suggest Wed 11/18 10am PT).
3) Provide a draft canary/fallback rollout playbook and cost estimate for Dedicated vs Hosted deployment options (Marissa — 11/20).

Attachments we’ll send in the follow-up: SLO tolerance matrix, one-pager on graceful degradation patterns, and a technical brief.

If I missed anything from the call, please call it out. Otherwise I’ll lock the deep-dive time once you confirm availability.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Asha Menon <asha@summitbank.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@summitbank.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-16T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Discovery follow-up: SLO tolerance & graceful degradation (Summit Bank)

Karthik — thanks for the clear summary. Confirming the points below and adding detail from our side.

Incident history (short):
- 2026-03-11: degraded model cache miss under heavy load — intermittent 502s for non-critical flows.
- 2026-09-03: region outage affecting primary API gateway — payments stalled for ~45 mins; fallback attempted but failed due to model variant mismatch and tokenization differences.
- 2026-10-22: partial throttling misconfiguration — spike in latency and 10% error rate for fraud-decisions for ~15 mins.

Our internal constraints and must-haves:
- Any fallback must be auditable and produce a traceable decision (no opaque "unknown" states).
- Security/compliance: all inference must not persist PII in logs; need KMS integration for keys if using private deployment.
- SLA expectation for negotiations: payment-critical path needs 99.9% monthly availability; other non-critical flows can be lower.

Success criteria (from our side):
- Deterministic degraded responses under component failure (e.g., return rule-based decision + a limited-score payload).
- Clear RCA artifacts within 48 hours for any production incident.
- Ability to failover to a regional replica + quantized smaller model that can run on cheaper capacity.

We’re available for the deep dive on Wed 11/18 10am PT; Tom and I will invite our infra lead (she’s on PTO but can join remotely if needed). I’ve attached the incident report from Sep 3 for context and linked our Jira tickets: https://summitbank.atlassian.net/browse/SUM-2321.

Thanks — Asha
VP, Digital Payments
Summit Bank

Attachments: incident-report-20260903.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-16T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: Draft SLO tolerance + fallback approach for Summit Bank

Karthik / Marissa — I sketched a first pass of the matrix and a one-pager for the deep dive. High-level recommendations (summary):
- Multi-tier fallback: primary model -> quantized variant (same weights, int8) -> distilled model (smaller architecture) -> rule-based decisioning. Each step must include transformation rules to keep tokenization compatibility.
- Region routing: keep warm replicas in secondary region; use health-check based immediate failover for payment-critical endpoints.
- Caching: persistent KV cache for payment session context; on failover, serve from last-known-good snapshot to avoid tokenization drift.
- Observability: tie SLO regressions to prompt-set checks and automatic rollback on canary failures.

I attached slo-tolerance-matrix.xlsx and graceful-deg-onepager.pdf. Cost estimate (very rough) attached separately — Dedicated capacity with quantized models looks ~30–45% cheaper at peak for their workload vs hosted bursts. We’ll refine in the deep dive.

Action: Karthik — confirm deep dive invite; Marissa — please prepare a short chart showing latency profiles for quantized vs full models.

Thanks,
Ben
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: slo-tolerance-matrix.xlsx, graceful-deg-onepager.pdf
